source_notes: Angola LNG's single liquefaction train at Soyo is compressed by two on-site GE gas-turbine-driven compression trains (mechanical drive, shaft power to the refrigeration/liquefaction compressors) under a long-term GE service agreement signed 2012. Upgraded to green this recovery pass: GE's OWN newsroom press release (a primary/vendor-primary source, sufficient alone per SOP) independently states the same 'two GE gas turbine-driven compression trains' finding as the previously-cited offshore-energy.biz trade-press article, and the two are independently authored/hosted documents (GE's own release vs. an independent trade publication), satisfying ≥2-independent-source corroboration as well. hardware_summary: GE PGT25+G4 DLE gas turbines (aeroderivative, LM2500-derived) mechanically driving GE 2BCL refrigeration compressors across Hilli Episeyo's four PRICO liquefaction trains (Black & Veatch/GE contract, GE Mark VIe controls, 8 anti-surge valves, 98.9% guaranteed availability) PLUS 2x Rolls-Royce Bergen B35:40V20AG gas-fueled reciprocating engines dedicated to on-board power generation (liquefaction-process power, vessel operations, crew hotel load). Two separate vendor equipment packages confirm both a mechanical-drive train and a dedicated generator set.
source_notes: Hilli Episeyo (Golar's converted Moss LNG carrier, moored ~10km offshore Kribi, 2.4 mtpa PRICO design) has TWO confirmed on-site gas-fired systems from its original 2014-2017 conversion: (1) GE PGT25+G4 DLE gas turbines mechanically driving GE 2BCL compressors across the four liquefaction trains (Black & Veatch/GE contract, announced May 2015), and (2) two dedicated Rolls-Royce Bergen B35:40V20AG all-gas reciprocating engines supplying the vessel's own power generation for the liquefaction process, vessel operation, and crew (Keppel/Rolls-Royce contract, announced March 2015). This resolves the prior shard's INSUFFICIENT finding, which searched startup/operations coverage but not the 2015 equipment-order press releases from the conversion program itself.

hardware_summary: Energos Winter (sole operating unit) runs steam turbine propulsion machinery; steam-turbine LNG carriers of this vintage use dual-fuel boilers that burn boil-off gas to raise steam for both propulsion and shipboard turbo-generators.
source_notes: Damietta FSRU's sole unit, Energos Winter, is a moored former LNG-carrier FSRU on steam-turbine machinery. Steam LNG carriers of this class run dual-fuel boilers burning boil-off gas (as well as fuel oil) to generate the steam that (via turbo-generators, standard on this ship type) supplies the vessel's own electrical/hotel load and regas-plant power while moored - this is captive gas power under the FSRU-onboard convention. Confidence is yellow because the gas-burning capability is established by vessel-class engineering convention plus the operator's own 'steam turbine propulsion' label, not by a vessel-specific statement of boiler fuel.

source_notes: SEGAS's single LNG train (T1, operating) is driven by two GE Frame 7 gas turbines in the Split MRTM refrigerant-compressor configuration - classic mechanical-drive captive gas power, described in detail in the plant's own conference paper. hardware_summary: 3x open-cycle gas turbine generating units, 62 MWe combined design capacity, commissioned 1977, operated by Sirte Oil Co at the Marsa al Burayqah site (coordinates essentially coincide with the LNG terminal's own).
source_notes: A 62 MWe, 3-unit open-cycle gas turbine power plant at Marsa al Burayqah, commissioned 1977 and operated by Sirte Oil Co — the same 100% owner GEM records for the Marsa El Brega LNG terminal — sits at coordinates matching the terminal's own (30.40N/19.60E, within ~1 km). This reads as the terminal's own captive generation. Still single-source for the plant's specific existence/rating (Global Energy Observatory) despite a genuine recovery-pass effort; confidence remains yellow rather than green. However, the host-trap sanity check requested for this pass now has independent support: Wikipedia's 'Sirte Oil Company' article (not GEM-derived, not the GEO source) independently confirms SOC operates the WHOLE Marsa el Brega industrial complex as a single entity — both the LNG plant ('processed about 900 million cubic meters per year... as of 2005') and the adjoining refinery (10,000 bbl/d) — consistent with, though not itself proof of, a single Sirte Oil Co-owned generating plant serving the complex rather than belonging to a separate tenant.

hardware_summary: As-designed replica of Coral Sul FLNG's topsides: aeroderivative-gas-turbine-driven turbo-compression trains (mechanical drive, refrigeration) plus separate aeroderivative-gas-turbine-driven turbo-generation units (electric generators) — vendor/model not yet separately announced for this hull.
source_notes: Coral North (vessel 'Coral Norte', launched Jan 2026 at Samsung Heavy's Geoje yard) is Eni's second Coral-field FLNG, EPCIC'd by the same Technip Energies/JGC/Samsung Heavy (TJS-style) consortium that built Coral Sul. TechnipFMC's own release says it will 'leverage our experience gained from the successful delivery of Coral South... by replicating our proven playbook.' Coral Sul's confirmed design carries both mechanical-drive refrigeration turbines and dedicated turbo-generation power units (see next entry), so the as-designed captive power finding on this proposed/pre-startup (targeted 2028) sister project is a YES on design, not yet independently confirmed equipment-by-equipment.

hardware_summary: 4x turbo-compression trains (aeroderivative gas turbines driving centrifugal refrigeration compressors, mechanical drive) + 4x turbo-generation units (aeroderivative gas turbines driving GE Power Conversion electric generators), all supplied by Baker Hughes (a GE company)/BHGE Nuovo Pignone, assembled/tested at BHGE's Massa (Italy) facility; plus BOG/booster compressors down to -180°C.
source_notes: Coral Sul FLNG (operating, Eni-operated, 3.4 Mtpa) carries on-board captive power: Baker Hughes/GE supplied 4 turbo-compression trains (mechanical drive for mixed-refrigeration compressors) plus 4 separate turbo-generation units in which aeroderivative gas turbines drive GE Power Conversion electric generators. This is both a mechanical-drive finding (True) and a genuine on-site electricity-generation finding (power_generation), so category is the mixed case.

hardware_summary: 6x Siemens Energy SGT-800 industrial gas turbine generators (54 MW each, 39% gross efficiency, dry low-emission combustion) for on-site power generation, plus 4x Siemens Energy centrifugal compressors for boil-off-gas service.
source_notes: TotalEnergies' onshore Mozambique LNG (Area 1, Afungi, Cabo Delgado) plant has confirmed dedicated on-site electricity generation: six Siemens Energy SGT-800 gas turbines (54 MW each, ~324 MW aggregate) explicitly for 'low-emissions onsite power generation,' per both the original 2020 contract announcement and a 2026 restart-coverage article. This matches the GOGPT-side 'Mozambique LNG power station' record (324 MW, 6.9 km away) almost exactly.

hardware_summary: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries 120 MW dual-shaft H-100 gas turbines as mechanical drivers for the main liquefaction (refrigeration) compressors, supplied together with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Compressor (MCO) main liquefaction compressors, for Rovuma LNG Phase 1 (two trains, Air Products AP-X process, ≥7.6 Mtpa).
source_notes: The onshore Rovuma LNG project (Mozambique Rovuma Venture — the successor entity to the original ExxonMobil-led Area 4 onshore development, adjacent to but distinct from TotalEnergies' Mozambique LNG/Area 1 site) has a confirmed 2019 equipment order for Mitsubishi Heavy Industries 120 MW H-100 dual-shaft gas turbines as mechanical drivers for its liquefaction compressors — mechanical-drive captive gas power, which counts under the current definition regardless of the fact no separate electricity-generation figure was found.

source_notes: Nigeria LNG's Bonny Island plant runs its own on-site gas-turbine power generation (ten gas turbine generators, combined >320 MW per NS Energy Business/GlobalData) in addition to four heavy-duty gas turbines driving the refrigeration compressors (Baker Hughes long-term service agreement announcement). This is a mixed mechanical-drive-plus-generation site: a documented YES with mechanical flagged True.
